subject.title: fix(codex): add WebSocket handshake timeout to app-server transport

question: Should a fixed 30-second Codex WebSocket handshake deadline proceed only after direct sibling-Codex inspection and a real app-server run confirm the timeout and failure behavior?
rationale: The mechanism matches the `ws` contract, but OpenClaw policy requires direct Codex source inspection, and a fixed deadline creates a small intentional availability cutoff that synthetic loopback proof alone cannot fully settle.

options.title: Require Codex runtime proof
options.body: Refresh the branch, inspect sibling Codex source, and capture a redacted real app-server stalled-handshake or equivalent diagnostic run before merge.

options.title: Accept loopback proof
options.body: Accept the upstream `ws` contract and current loopback transcript as sufficient evidence for the fixed 30-second cutoff.

recommendation.title: Require Codex runtime proof
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, inspect sibling Codex source, and capture a redacted real app-server stalled-handshake or equivalent diagnostic run before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged history identifies this person as the primary author and merger of the current Codex app-server lifecycle implementation.
